va-fx-commercial-gfa.title: Commercial districts: special exception above 40,000 sq ft
va-fx-commercial-gfa.description: In C-3 or C-4, a data center building over 40,000 sq ft of gross floor area needs a special exception. The Planning Commission hears the request first and makes a recommendation. The Board decides at a second hearing. The county estimates about six months from acceptance.

va-fx-industrial-gfa.title: Industrial districts: special exception above 80,000 sq ft
va-fx-industrial-gfa.description: In I-2, I-3 or I-4, a data center building over 80,000 sq ft of gross floor area needs a special exception. The Planning Commission hears the request first and makes a recommendation. The Board decides at a second hearing. The county estimates about six months from acceptance.

va-fx-setback.title: Residential setbacks for buildings and equipment
va-fx-setback.description: Keep the building at least 200 ft from an R-district lot line or a lot in residential use. Ground-mounted equipment needs 300 ft or the principal building between it and that line. Public street rights-of-way do not count as R districts. The Board may approve shorter distances by special exception.

va-fx-noise.title: Noise studies before site approval and occupancy
va-fx-noise.office: Fairfax County Zoning Administrator or designee
va-fx-noise.description: Submit a noise study before site plan approval. After construction, measure installed equipment at full load before the Nonresidential Use Permit is issued. Rezoning and special exception applications also need a study; qualifying projects at 100 MW or more must assess noise at homes and schools within 500 ft of the property boundary.
